quest.title: Someone Trustworthy
quest.description: It turns out that in order to reach the mysterious island, it is necessary to have a guide, one with whom mutual trust is shared...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Where the Springs Return: Act III
chapter.title: Journey to the Mysterious Island

talks.objective: Return to the People of the Springs

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After all we've been through recently, it sure feels good to come back to visit the People of the Springs!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a while since we last got in touch with Mualani. Wonder what she's up to now...

choices.text: Why don't we just ask her to be our guide?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Have Mualani be our guide? Ah, Paimon just remembered something... Do you remember that journey to the mysterious island that we were never able to complete?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's the one! Paimon remembers the chief of the People of the Springs told us that we must find a guide we could trust with our lives... That would make Mualani the perfect choice, wouldn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We can invite her to be our guide and set off for the island. As qualified adventurers, we should never give up!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're thinking about the treasure, aren't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we should always keep the treasure in mind, shouldn't we? C'mon, let's go find Mualani!

choices.text: She can take us on a tour of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Sorry, we don't carry any black swimming floaters here.

dialogues.speaker: Customer
dialogues.text: But why? Black floaters look really cool.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hmm... may I ask whether you've had some bad luck lately?

dialogues.speaker: Customer
dialogues.text: Uh, well yeah, sorta... The last pair of black floaters I bought ended up getting bitten by a Koholasaur. I nearly drowned... Which is why I want to buy some new ones.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I knew it. I specifically asked an expert from the Masters of the Night-Wind about this once. Black floaters bring bad luck!

dialogues.speaker: Customer
dialogues.text: R—Really?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Also... have you by any chance become a mosquito magnet? Or found yourself overheating, maybe even suffering a little heatstroke?

dialogues.speaker: Customer
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's exactly how I've been feeling! It's all starting to make sense now...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: In that case, I'd recommend either pink or blue swimming floaters. According to the experts, bright colors can not only lift your mood, but also bring good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I'll even offer you a discount if you'd like. Just see it as a way of celebrating your luck taking a turn for the better!

dialogues.speaker: Customer
dialogues.text: You'd really do that? Then... I'll take one of each!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You got it!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Well hello there, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Mualani!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good to see you again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was all that stuff you were saying just now really true? Do pink and blue floaters really bring good luck?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Of course! I know a friend who nearly drowned once, but because she was wearing blue floaters, a group of Koholasaurs came to the rescue and brought her back to shore!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, for real?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But let's get back to why you're here. Are you looking to buy some watersports products?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: C'mon, don't be strangers now! I can give you whatever you need, you are guests here, after all. It's only natural for me to give some gifts to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no! We actually came here to ask you to be our guide.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Well, you've come to the right person. So where do you wanna go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We want to visit the mysterious island from the legend!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: A trip to the mysterious island? Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you have any concerns, Mualani?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I assume you're already aware of how difficult the trip will be, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, your chief has already made that pretty clear!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But with our adventuring experience and with you as our guide, we'll definitely be able to reach the mysterious island!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Then, I'll have to explain some things to you first.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I learned all my skills as a guide from Uncle Nuu, and he's the best guide in the whole tribe. But, apparently, even he has never successfully reached the island.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: With a good guide to lead the way, a journey should usually be fun and pleasant. However, going to the mysterious island is different, and I don't know if I can guarantee that.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But since it's you two asking, I definitely won't refuse.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: It's just my duty as a guide to explain these things before I officially agree to go on the journey.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought that this would be a piece of cake for you... But it seems like we're actually asking a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon would feel really guilty to make a friend go through a bunch of trouble just for the sake of finding some treasure!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's not ideal...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Mualani...

dialogues.speaker: Seketo
dialogues.text: Whoa, what's the hurry?

dialogues.speaker: Suya
dialogues.text: C'mon, what're you waiting for? Koolau just got back to the tribe! I heard he found another underground ruin full of treasure!

dialogues.speaker: Seketo
dialogues.text: Oh, Koolau's back!? Wait for me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who's Koolau?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, he's currently ranked as the number one guide in the People of the Springs. Besides the tribe's first chief, he's the only other guide who's ever made it to the mysterious island.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: He's always out and about, so we don't get to see him often. Sounds like this is quite an occasion, though. Let's go check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Let me put up the closed sign first... Okay, come with me!

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: The crystals you asked for can only be found in caverns deeper than 500 meters underground. Here, have a look for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: As for the people you asked me to take along, they almost all got lost in a cave. Out of my sense of duty as a guide, I've brought them all back.

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: Next time, just save the trouble and let me go alone.

dialogues.speaker: Commissioner
dialogues.text: Indeed, well done.

dialogues.speaker: Seketo
dialogues.text: No wonder he's the best. I wouldn't dare to go more than 200 meters down into a cavern like that!

dialogues.speaker: Suya
dialogues.text: I wonder how much he made this time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, he really does sound like a super amazing guide. Do you think you could get some pointers from him, Mualani? Who knows, maybe he could save us some trouble on our trip to the mysterious island!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Koolau always treats his experience like trade secrets. He never tells anyone anything about being a guide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But one day, I'll also be able to reach the island.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: That's him, right? Do you really think you'll be able to get his help?

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Allow me to do the talking.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: You must be the top guide of your tribe. I have a commission that I hope you'd be willing to consider.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that guy sure looks familiar... Oh, aren't those two the scholars from Sumeru who were bitten by the Koholasaurs?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They also wanted to go to the mysterious island, right? Seems they've finally realized that they need a guide.

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: A commission? Since you've obviously heard about my abilities, have you also happened to hear about my rates? If you're not intimidated by the price, then we can talk.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Yes, I've looked into everything I need to know. As long as the trip is a success, then the commission fees won't be a problem.

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: Oh? And where is it you want to go?

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: The mysterious island.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just as Paimon thought...

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: But first, please don't misunderstand. I'm no tourist, I wish to visit the real place!

dialogues.speaker: Seketo
dialogues.text: You hear that? He wants to go to the island...

dialogues.speaker: Suya
dialogues.text: In that case, Koolau's the only one for the job. But the journey to the island requires a lot more than just a guide, right?

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: Since you want to visit the real mysterious island, then I'm sure you've also heard about the requirement for our trip, right?

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Yes, I know. According to the legend, only those who are willing to entrust their lives to one another will be able to reach the island together.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: I must reach that island, even if that means putting my life in someone else's hands. I have made up my mind!

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: Don't waste your words on me. Way I see it, the requirement is just a way to weed out those who do not have the skills to reach the island by themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Y—You...

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: You say you'd put your life in somebody else's hands? Ridiculous. Even if someone were to trust me with their life, they'd just be another burden.

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: Let's look at it the other way around. Why would I place my life in the hands of someone whose abilities are far below mine? That is what the legend is really hinting at here.

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: Many guides in the tribe have received commissions like this, only to end up bogged down by their incompetent clients long before reaching the destination.

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: How do you think I reached the mysterious island? I made it because I chose to go alone.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Well, um... I'm different. I'm no ordinary tourist!

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: That doesn't make much of a difference to me. You'll give up half way at best, which is a waste of my time, and a waste of your commission fees.

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: I can tell you're just looking to explore something new. If that's the case, then you can find another guide in the tribe. For example...

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: Nuu's student over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's up with that guy's attitude? Paimon takes back everything nice she said about him!

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: I have things to do now. Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hold on, Koolau!

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: What's wrong? I'm only introducing a potential client to you because I know your teacher. In fact, I'd say it's quite the opportunity.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Never mind that for now. I don't agree with your views on the island! Uncle Nuu taught me that—

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: I know, you're just the same as him. You both obviously hope to prove yourselves, but still think that you have to follow the legend to the letter... waiting for a cumbersome client to find you before even trying to set off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mualani...

dialogues.speaker: Koolau
dialogues.text: The rare ores I brought back are proof that I've been to the island. But as for Nuu? Where's his proof? Why don't you wait until he's actually found the island before you start using his views to refute me?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After Koolau leaves, the crowd begins to disperse.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I'm really sorry, I just wanted to take you to see what the excitement was all about... I wasn't planning on getting into an argument with him again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That Koolau seemed to harbor some kind of grudge against you, Mualani. Or maybe your teacher?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I know... Quite an impressive achievement for my teacher, huh? Even the best guide in the tribe can't stop talking about him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought you would be more upset.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Of course not! Uncle Nuu has also argued with Koolau before. I've already heard the same words several times now.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But it's hard to prove anything to him unless you've actually been to the island.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You also really hope to reach the island, right, Mualani?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's right. It's just that I've always seen the journey as something super important and not to be taken lightly. I was really surprised when you asked me to be your guide today.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Ah! After telling you about all the dangers with such a serious face, I didn't make you think that you're causing me trouble, did I?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, Paimon did think about taking our invite back.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: No, please don't do that! Actually, that is also a part of what Uncle Nuu taught me as a guide. The difficulty of the trip is the very first thing that needs to be clearly laid out to the group.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Ahem... "If you want a chance of reaching the destination together, you must first reach a consensus on the amount of effort that will be required."

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I always felt that my teacher is no less skilled than Koolau, but Uncle Nuu has never been to the island, so Koolau always uses that to push us down.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So, as Uncle Nuu's student, I've always wanted to complete the trip to prove his skills. It's a pity that I've never had the chance...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But don't you have that chance now, Mualani? If you'd agree to be our guide, we're completely willing to trust you with our lives!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #With the help of the renowned {NICKNAME} and {M#his}{F#her} trusty companion, you'll definitely be able to find the mysterious island. Then you can come back and teach that Koolau a lesson!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Aw, Paimon... C'mon, bring it in!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, you're making Paimon blush...!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Alrighty then, if we're gonna go, we should start preparing right away. I've already had the plans for this trip written out for some time. Come with me!

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Ahem!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's that scholar guy. Paimon almost forgot he was still here...

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Scholar guy? My name is Viramdra. Please use it!

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: #I didn't expect to see you again, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and it's that lady, too! Hello again!

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: Excuse me... Miss Guide. Since we've been referred to you, would it be okay for us to join your journey?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I'm Mualani. Just call me by my name.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: As for whether or not you can come along, I'm sure you've already heard the requirements. We've only just met, and I'm not sure you're cut out for this trip. The path to the mysterious island is a grueling one.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: I admit that after coming to Natlan, I've encountered many things outside of my field of expertise. It's understandable you're worried that we'll slow you down, so how about this?

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: We'll set off with you as ordinary travel companions, and I'll pay you the usual commission fees, but we won't officially be your clients.

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: In other words, you needn't shoulder the responsibility of being our guide. And even if something were to happen to us, your reputation as a guide won't be tarnished as a result. How does that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: If you accompany us, then you are a member of the team. I could never agree to such a careless deal... Don't tell me you think I'm the same kind of person as Koolau?

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: So you still refuse... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: Fine. Karya, I'll put the Mora for the return trip in your backpack. Without a guide, the road ahead may be dangerous, so please don't follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: Viramdra...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now he wants to go alone? Why is this guy so obsessed with that island?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Wait, please don't do this in front of a guide! I can't let a tourist go on some dangerous journey all alone. Even my sweet mom would give me a harsh scolding if I ever let you do that.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry for the trouble, really...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't say that. Although it'd be inappropriate to bring along two strangers I just met, there is another solution.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: How about this... Let's meet up tomorrow morning at the monument near the tribe's southeastern slope. I'll see you there!

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: So you've decided to accept my offer?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: No, my plan is to use some of our time together to turn you from strangers into friends... the kind we can trust with our lives!

dialogues.speaker: Viramdra
dialogues.text: ...That's your plan? Very well then.

dialogues.speaker: Karya
dialogues.text: Wonderful! On behalf of both Viramdra and I, thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pretty sure only Mualani could come up with a plan like that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yep, that's Mualani for you!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We need to get started on our preparations. Come with me!

talks.objective: Accompany Mualani to the fishing shop

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Heya, Lafa! I've got some business for ya!

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: We've been over this before... the name's Yelafath.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I know, it's just that "Lafa" sounds so much cuter!

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Well, since you're the customer here, I guess whatever floats your boat...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I need a camping tent with all the accessories... Only the best you've got!

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Another commission, huh? Just so you know, a full tent according to your standards is gonna be pricey. Is your client covering the bill?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How much are we talkin'?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't worry about the costs, I'll take care of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, but, that's not right!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're the clients, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Ahem! Let's make this clear, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. We're not working together like this is a hired commission, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, no... we're traveling as close friends who trust each other with anything!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's what I thought! Honestly, I can be a little picky when it comes to camping equipment, and I don't want my friends to be paying for me. But don't worry, it's not that expensive.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We're ready, Lafa!

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Your total is 200,000 Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't that still a lot for you, Mualani?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Just imagine us in the wilderness, okay? We can either sleep out in the open, tired and weary, or simply spend a week's worth of pocket money and completely solve that problem. I'd say that's a great deal!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You call that a week's worth of pocket money? Are you rich, Mualani?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's not important! We still need to buy some equipment from another store. Come with me!

talks.objective: Accompany Mualani to the instrument store

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Afternoon, Uncle An!

dialogues.speaker: Anchieta
dialogues.text: You call me "uncle," but I'm old enough to be your grandfather, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Because you're still young, Uncle An! Hey, can you help me find something kinda rare? I can negotiate the price, what do you say?

dialogues.speaker: Anchieta
dialogues.text: Alright, what're you looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: A record player... specifically, the kind that's convenient to take camping.

dialogues.speaker: Anchieta
dialogues.text: Ah, that model is pretty rare, indeed. I thought it'd be nice to keep it as a prized collectible in the shop...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Ahem, Uncle An?

dialogues.speaker: Anchieta
dialogues.text: *coughing* Just don't break it, okay? I'll even buy it back from ya when you're done with it!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Thanks, Uncle An!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A record player? Does that mean we need to buy some records, too?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yep! And that's our next stop!

talks.objective: Accompany Mualani to the record store

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hey, Pakaa Pakaa!

dialogues.speaker: Pakaa Nui
dialogues.text: Mualani? Have you finally decided to release a record of your own?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You'd be the first I'd sign with if I ever did, but not today... I just want to buy a record, the one you've been keeping from customers and listening to in secret.

dialogues.speaker: Pakaa Nui
dialogues.text: Huh? That's a pretty rare record, you know... Besides, I haven't even finished listening to that one yet.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Maybe I can think of a way to connect you with a friend from the Masters of the Night-Wind to release a record...

dialogues.speaker: Pakaa Nui
dialogues.text: Whoa, then we could produce some really wild tunes! You've got a deal!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Nice! That's the record also accounted for.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do we need it for, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Well, I asked a friend from the Masters of the Night-Wind for some advice once, and apparently, playing this song at night is an effective way to keep travelers safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that really a thing? Well, if it doesn't cost much, that's a nice way to make the trip a little more pleasant...

dialogues.speaker: Pakaa Nui
dialogues.text: You know how it goes, Mualani. 20,000 Mora for this record — that's the best I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Deal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Mualani really is rich!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That should be about everything we need to buy. Next is... Oh, I'm getting kinda nervous.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Mualani?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Next, I need to find my teacher, and get the map to the island.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Besides the legend left by the first chief, there's also a map. Well, not just a regular map, it's more like a treasure map...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: It's full of strange symbols, almost like it's a part of a big puzzle. Guides must draw from their experience to decipher the map's meaning and understand the route.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: The chief made several copies of the map, and distributed them to the first members of the tribe. The copies were to be passed down to future generations, so usually a teacher will pass their copy to their student.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Which brings us to today... the day I officially ask Uncle Nuu for his copy of the map.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, hearing that is also making Paimon feel a little nervous! Sounds like it must be a pretty serious moment.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yes, but the thought of having you two by my side somehow makes me feel a lot better. We won't let Uncle Nuu down, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Let's go and find him together, hehe!

talks.objective: Accompany Mualani as she meets her teacher

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Afternoon, Uncle Nuu! I have a big surprise for you!

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: A surprise... Then you must be here to finally pick up the map.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Ah, you saw right through me as always...

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: Did you forget that you had mentioned these two to me before? The ones who went to the Night Kingdom with you... In some sense, you could say that you've already trusted each other with your lives.

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: It's just that... my feelings are a little complicated now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Do you think that I'm still not ready yet, Uncle Nuu?

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: No, I believe you are the best guide in your generation. It's just that... I'm not ready yet.

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: After all, the journey to the mysterious island is no easy feat for any guide of the People of the Springs. I'm still a little worried...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, with our help, Mualani will definitely be able to find the mysterious island!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yeah, this time, I'll definitely be able to prove that Koolau is no better than Uncle Nuu!

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: Don't misunderstand. Since you've made up your minds, I won't try to stop you. It's just... please listen to your teacher's words once more, Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: Our mission as guides has never been to prove anything. There is only one thing we must do... guide tourists safely to their destination.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: ...I understand, Uncle Nuu.

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: In that case, you may have the map. Also, take this with you.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: It's a talisman. Take good care of it. You must return it to me when you get back from the mysterious island.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Was this made with Spinel Fruit? Hmm, for some reason, this doesn't look like a regular Spinel Fruit to me...

dialogues.speaker: Nuu
dialogues.text: Right, which is precisely why it's so effective.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You really know me best, Uncle Nuu.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Alright. {NICKNAME} and Paimon, tomorrow we'll set off. Make sure you get some good rest tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, Paimon can't wait for another adventure!
